$comment: SPOKEN DIGITS — the PII class no gate in this system could see (#747 leg (a)).
WHY IT EXISTS. `pseudonymize.py` masks a phone number by its SHAPE: `_PHONE_RE` wants 9-13
digits, `_RESIDUAL_DIGITS_RE` wants 7+ consecutive ones. Both are Unicode-aware, so Devanagari
numerals (०-९) are already covered — measured, not assumed. What neither can see is a
worker SPEAKING their number: saarika returns 'nau aath saat...' as WORDS, which carry no digit
characters at all, so every net in the gateway passes them through and the number reaches the
LLM boundary intact.
THE THRESHOLD IS BORROWED, NOT INVENTED. A run of 9-13 digit tokens is 'phone-shaped' here
because that is exactly what `_PHONE_RE` already decided for numerals (Indian mobiles are 10;
a country/STD prefix reaches 12-13). Reusing the reviewed number means there is ONE definition
of phone-shaped in this service rather than two that can drift apart.
WHAT THE THRESHOLD PROTECTS, which matters more than what it catches. Digit words are ordinary
Hinglish speech: 'do saal' is two years, 'saade teen saal' is three and a half, 'char logon ki
team'. Those are runs of ONE. A redactor that fired on any digit word would silently destroy
the answers this whole form exists to capture — experience, team size, shift numbers — and it
would look like a privacy win while doing it. The permitted cases are tested as hard as the
forbidden ones.
NOT IN lexicon_data/. That directory is mirrored BYTE-FOR-BYTE into packages/profiling-lexicon
and parity-tested, because TypeScript reads it too. This lexicon is privacy-boundary data that
only this service uses, so it sits beside its module like app/tts_data/ does — adding it to the
mirror would create a parity obligation for a file the TypeScript side never opens.
'no' IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the 9 list. It is English negation and a Hinglish filler; the
run-length threshold would usually save it, but a word that common has no business being a
digit token at all. 'nau' is the Hindi nine and is unambiguous.
$comment_threshold: Inclusive bounds on the number of digit tokens in a run, mirroring `_PHONE_RE`'s {8,12}
repetition of a leading digit (i.e. 9-13 digits total).
$comment_placeholder: A FIXED token, not a numbered one. `pseudonymize.py` numbers its masks ([PHONE_1]) because it
correlates entities across a document; this runs earlier, on one transcript, and carries no
counter. It is also digit-free by construction, so it passes through the gateway downstream
without being re-masked or tripping the residual-digit net.
